messages:
jamie: Quick heads-up — after the kernel-selector tweak on canary we see long-seq tenants getting starved in the batching layer. Queue time for >1k-token requests jumped. Profiling snippet pasted below.
```
p50_queue_time: 12ms -> 34ms
p95_queue_time: 110ms -> 420ms
avg_batch_size: 4.3 -> 2.1
kv_hit_rate: 0.87 -> 0.62
long_tenant_queued_count: +230
```
Anyone else seeing this pattern?

sara: yup, I saw the same in the nightly perf dashboard. Looks like the new token-budget target is aggressively preferring short sequences which collapses mixed batches. Short requests get into fast-path more often and end up consuming credits.

anand: Summary from my offline profiler: rotor selects microbatches by token-budget per-lane. After tightening the alpha it hands more slots to lanes with low median seq len. That reduces opportunity to coalesce long + short which hurts long latency and KV warmup for long tenants.

li: two ideas: 1) add a tiny negative bias to the short-lane score when a lane's recent kv_hit_rate < threshold, to force warmup samples for cold tenants; 2) introduce a "min-long-share" per window so long sequences get guaranteed batch slots.

quentin: +1. Also proposal to smooth the token credit refill: current refill is bursty (big jumps on idle) — change to exponential moving average so short request storms don't empty reservoir for long sequences.

jamie: Concrete change set I propose for an experiment:
- revert token_budget_alpha from 0.58 -> 0.72 (less aggressive favoring of short).
- add min_long_share = 0.08 (meaning at least 8% of mini-batches in 30s window must include a long-seq tenant)
- kv_preemptive_warmup: sample X long requests per N batches when kv_hit_rate < 0.7
- refill smoothing: credit_refill_alpha = 0.15 (EMA)

perf-bot: Canary run link: https://perf.redwood/canary/230987-canary-rotor-2 (metrics posted) :chart_with_upwards_trend:

li: example config snippet for the batcher guardrails: 
```yaml
batcher:
  token_budget_alpha: 0.72
  min_long_share: 0.08
  kv_preemptive_warmup:
    enabled: true
    sample_every: 30  # batches
    min_samples: 2
  credit_refill_alpha: 0.15
```

sara: nice. Metrics to watch: long_seq_p95_queue_time, per-tenant starvation_count (defined as queued > 200ms), kv_hit_rate_by_tenant, avg_batch_fill_ratio, and fairness_index (we already have a Gini-style metric).

anand: for canary, let's A/B: control = current rotor, variant = rotor+min_long_share+kv_warmup. Run 2h windows during UTC morning traffic. Instrument trace ids for any long requests that hit fast-path vs delayed.

quentin: rollout plan: feature flag gated. Start 1% traffic, collect metrics, then 10%, 30%, rollback if long_seq_p95 increases by >10% or starvation_count increases by >20%.

jamie: action items:
- anand to land flag + config (ETA 4h)
- li to add kv-warmup sampling hook (ETA EOD)
- sara to add dashboard panels + alerts (ETA 2h)
- quentin to own canary rollout and automation (ETA this afternoon)
